title: In 1912, an Alaskan Volcano Erupted 30 Times Bigger Than St. Helens

scenes.text: In 1912, Alaska erupted 30 times bigger than Mount St. Helens.
Novarupta erupted for three days in June 1912.
The ash cloud shot 20 miles high.
A hundred miles away on Kodiak Island, ash piled over a foot deep and collapsed roofs.
The sky went dark, and people could barely breathe for three days.
The blasts were reported as far away as Juneau, about 750 miles off.
Thirty times St. Helens, and most people have never heard of it.

description:
In June 1912, Novarupta in Alaska released about 30 times more magma than Mount St. Helens did in 1980.
Ash collapsed roofs on Kodiak Island, and explosions were reported as far away as Juneau.
Had you heard of it?
first_comment: Had you ever heard of Novarupta before this?
